label: early copy-phase steps (recall 1-2) of short sequences (L<=4)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase. It never fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step, or on recall_idx 0, and only on tokens that are being repeated (in_first = 0). The core is short sequences: when L is 3 or 4 it fires on the 2nd and 3rd copy outputs (recall_idx 1-2) with about 88% precision, and these steps hold about 70% of the activation mass. The strongest activations are all at L=3 right after <DEL> (e.g. c b v <DEL> [c] [b]). The last copy step of an L=4 sequence (recall 3) is mostly inactive. The other ~30% of mass is weak, diffuse firing in longer sequences (L>=5), mostly at recall_idx 1-5 and somewhat more often at L=9. Here it is mildly enriched for input tokens r and d, but no clean rule captures it. Token identity barely modulates firing in the core case.
